assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene opened a new platform in which a single tunable parameter (twist angle) controls flat-band physics, correlated insulators and superconductivity; it is original, conceptually clear and has spawned moire materials as a whole field.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the flat bands at the magic angle; Jarillo-Herrero's group delivered the decisive experimental discovery of correlated insulating states and superconductivity. This theory-plus-experiment split fits a three-way prize naturally. Other experimental groups contributed related work, which I cannot fully weigh from the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Within roughly seven years the key results have been reproduced by many independent laboratories and extended to other moire systems, so the core phenomenology is well confirmed; timing seems right.
uncertainties: The microscopic origin of the superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene is still debated, so recognition would rest on the platform and correlated states rather than a settled mechanism.
Whether the prize should credit the experimental discovery alone or also the prediction is a judgment call.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall and quantum anomalous Hall effects introduced a new classification of electronic matter with robust edge states; the concept is deep, general and has lasting influence across condensed matter, photonics and materials.
assessment.attribution: Kane (with Mele) supplied the decisive theory of the quantum spin Hall state; Molenkamp's group observed it in HgTe quantum wells; Xue's group realised the quantum anomalous Hall effect. The three-name set spans theory, QSH experiment and QAH experiment, but omits Mele, Bernevig/Zhang and Hasan, which makes the credit contentious.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently for well over a decade across many materials and techniques; interpretation is stable. If anything the recognition is overdue.
uncertainties: Credit is contested: Mele, Hasan, and the Zhang and Bernevig predictions are not in this exact set, and the longlist contains a competing overlapping entry (B040).
Because this is a compound discovery, the QAH part may deserve separate treatment from the QSH part.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Fluctuation theorems are exact relations for work and entropy production far from equilibrium, extending the second law to individual stochastic trajectories. They are conceptually clean and have shaped stochastic thermodynamics, single-molecule biophysics and the study of small systems; this is close to my own field and I rate it highly on originality and clarity.
assessment.attribution: Evans, Cohen and Morriss provided the early fluctuation theorem; Jarzynski the work relation; Crooks the detailed fluctuation relation. Others, notably Gallavotti and Cohen, Kurchan, Lebowitz and Spohn, and Bustamante for experiments, are not in this credited set, so the allocation is genuinely unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Experimentally verified in RNA-hairpin pulling, colloidal and single-electron systems by several independent groups, and the theory is stable and widely used. Timing is reasonable, though the impact is more conceptual than technological.
uncertainties: Attribution is the main obstacle: priority between Evans-Searles, Gallavotti-Cohen, Jarzynski and Crooks is distributed over more people than three.
The Physics prize has been cautious about statistical-mechanics results with indirect technological impact.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Direct observation of Anderson localization of matter waves in controlled disorder realises a half-century-old fundamental prediction and makes it possible to study localization quantitatively, free of the interactions and decoherence that limit electronic systems.
assessment.attribution: The Aspect group (Billy et al.) and the Inguscio-Modugno group (Roati et al., quasi-periodic potentials) reported the observations in 2008. Fairly clean experimental credit; the theory belongs to Anderson, who is already recognised, and to later contributors such as Lagendijk or Wiersma for light, who are not in this set.
assessment.maturity: Independently reproduced by two groups with different disorder types and later extended to 3D and many-body localization; stable and mature, though the later excitement is more about follow-on directions than the 2008 result itself.
uncertainties: Overlap in spirit with earlier recognition of Anderson and of cold-atom Nobel prizes could make the committee consider it incremental.
Optical and acoustic localization experiments by others complicate the claim of first observation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit quantum electrodynamics is the architecture behind superconducting quantum processors: strong coupling of artificial atoms to microwave resonators allows readout, control and entanglement of qubits. Impact on quantum technology and fundamental quantum optics is large and growing.
assessment.attribution: Blais, Huang, Wallraff, Girvin and Schoelkopf proposed the circuit-QED scheme and Wallraff and colleagues demonstrated strong coupling in 2004. The three credited names are sensible, though Girvin and Devoret overlap with other prize-relevant superconducting-circuit work.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed widely and replicated by many groups, with now-standard use in industry; mature, though it comes shortly after the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits, which may affect timing.
uncertainties: Overlap with the earlier superconducting-circuit Nobel recognition and with Girvin's and Devoret's contributions makes the allocation uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Detection of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos with IceCube opened neutrino astronomy at TeV-PeV energies, including the evidence of a diffuse flux, the blazar TXS 0506+056 and the Galactic plane; a large and clearly articulated discovery.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led IceCube; Karle is credited as a leading figure. The instrument is the work of a large collaboration, so naming individuals is difficult, and other leaders may deserve consideration; I cannot judge from the supplied credit alone.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux is established at high significance, while source identification (beyond TXS 0506+056 and NGC 1068) is still emerging; maturity is solid for the discovery but the astrophysical interpretation is still developing.
uncertainties: Collaboration-scale discovery with an ambiguous individual allocation.
Source attribution of the bulk of the flux is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realise clean, tunable many-body Hamiltonians such as the Bose-Hubbard model and the superfluid to Mott-insulator transition, enabling quantum simulation of strongly correlated matter with single-site resolution; a conceptually strong bridge between statistical physics and atomic physics.
assessment.attribution: Zoller and colleagues proposed the Hubbard-model realisation; Greiner and Bloch observed the Mott transition and developed quantum gas microscopy. Cirac is also in the credited set but Zoller is the better-supported theory choice here; Hansch, Jaksch and Gross are not credited, so the allocation is open.
assessment.maturity: Replicated by many groups and now a mature platform, though quantum advantage for open problems is still developing; recognition is timely but overlaps with earlier cold-atom prizes.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier recognition of ultracold atoms may count against it.
The credited set mixes theory proposals and experiments, and some key contributors are missing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamical mean-field theory is the leading non-perturbative framework for strongly correlated electrons, exact in infinite dimensions, and combined with density-functional theory it is the workhorse for Mott physics and correlated materials.
assessment.attribution: Metzner and Vollhardt introduced the infinite-dimension limit, Georges and Kotliar built the DMFT mapping onto an impurity model, and Muller-Hartmann and Jarrell contributed; the credited three is plausible but Metzner is missing.
assessment.maturity: The framework is mature and widely validated against experiments and numerics, though predictive success is approximate in finite dimensions; timing is acceptable, but Nobel recognition of computational methods is rare.
uncertainties: Method rather than a single discovery; Metzner and others are absent from the credited set.
Committee tradition on theoretical methods is a concern.
